answer: The place I would like to describe is the riverside near my home in Sirajganj, beside the Jamuna river, which has always been a favourite spot of mine. It is only a short rickshaw ride from our flat, along the embankment on the edge of town. I try to go there two or three times a week, usually in the early evening once I have finished work. There is something deeply [[calming]] about sitting by the water and watching the sun set over it. The gentle sound of the current is wonderfully [[soothing]], and it seems to wash away the stress of daily life. I usually go for a slow walk along the bank, or simply sit with a cup of tea from one of the little stalls and let my mind wander. Sometimes I watch the fishing boats coming in, or children playing near the water's edge. What I love most is how [[tranquil]] it is compared to the noise of the town centre. There is often a cool breeze coming off the water, which is a blessing in the heat, especially in the sticky weeks before the monsoon. Of course, the river has another side too; in the rainy season it swells enormously, and [[riverbank erosion]] has cost many local families their land over the years. Perhaps that is why I respect it as much as I love it. Honestly, being near water has a [[therapeutic]] effect on me that is hard to explain. It is my favourite place to think, and I always leave feeling refreshed.

followUps.answer: Yes, quite a lot, especially in the evenings and on holidays. Families come to enjoy the breeze and young people gather to chat, but if you walk a little further along the bank it becomes much quieter.

followUps.q: Has the riverside changed since you were a child?
followUps.answer: Yes, a fair bit. The embankment has been strengthened, and there are more tea stalls and lights now. It is busier than before, but the view across the water is exactly the same.

note: He lives in Sirajganj, so 'whenever I visit home' and 'noise of the city' fixed; added how often, tea and boats, the river's destructive side; new mark 'riverbank erosion'.
